title: Edge Signal Cartographer: Cross-provider Latency & Feature Drift Investigation
creator: Ava Patel
body:
Summary:
Run a lightweight continuous telemetry program to map cross-provider latency surfaces, emergent feature drift, and short-lived outage/degeneration events that materially affect Redwood customers. The goal is an operational feed (weekly digest + alerting) that product, SRE, sales, and procurement can use to make deployment, routing, and procurement decisions.

Background and motivation:
- We observe surface-level signals from partners and field reports but lack a structured lane that combines synthetic workloads, marketplace metadata, and curated customer telemetry.
- Competitive providers increasingly change model behavior via fast variant deployments; customers experience intermittent regressions that are hard to attribute.
- A compact telemetry feed will lower reaction time for fallback policy changes and improve sales and SRE conversations.

Primary goals:
1) Produce a repeatable weekly "Edge Signal Card" summarizing regional latency percentiles, transient outages, and emerging API/feature deltas (e.g., function-calling, streaming anomalies).
2) Surface drift windows (time ranges where quality or latency materially deviated vs baseline) with suggested mitigation (route change, model variant fallback, or cache policy tweak).
3) Provide evidence packages for sales and procurement when customers request SLA-exception or assistance.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In scope: Hosted public provider endpoints + major open model inference endpoints (NA/EU regions); synthetic probes (short-context and long-context), marketplace listing scrapes (release notes, quant notes), and selected customer-reported incidents.
- Out of scope: Deep model fidelity evaluation (LLM quality benchmarks) and on-prem private deployment telemetry in this phase.

Deliverables:
- Weekly Edge Signal Card (PDF + Slack digest) with 6 prioritized signals and recommended action per signal.
- Back-end collector: lightweight probe runner (k8s CronJob prototype) + aggregator dashboard (Console prototype link).
- Evidence kit for each signal: raw probe logs, example customer traces (redacted), and suggested mitigation playbook snippets.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Weekly cards produced with >=90% data completeness for targeted regions.
- Time from first detection to product owner notification <= 24h for high-severity signals.
- Two sales/procurement requests resolved using the evidence kit without engineering time > 2 hours.

Milestones & timeline:
- Week 1 (2025-02-17 to 2025-02-23): Define probe matrix and provider list. Create initial CronJob skeleton and proof-of-concept runner.
- Week 2: Onboard synthetic workloads (short/long context), implement basic aggregator, begin marketplace scraping.
- Week 3: Populate first internal card; run internal review, iterate UI copy and action templates.
- Week 4-6: Harden alerting, integrate customer incident ingestion process, pilot with two SRE/oncall rotations.

Key stakeholders:
- Product lead: Ava Patel
- Assignee/PM partner: Liam O'Connor
- SRE liaison: Priya Malhotra
- Research/Applied ML: Daniel Kim (probe design)
- Sales enablement: Maria Gonzalez

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated weekly card generated and posted to #market-intel channel for 4 consecutive weeks.
- For any high-severity signal, evidence kit attachment is available and verified by SRE.
- Documented playbook (Confluence link) with decision thresholds and rollback suggestions.

Risks and trade-offs:
- False positives from noisy probes: mitigate by cross-validating with marketplace and customer telemetry and adding minimum signal persistence window.
- Provider TOS / scraping limits: prefer public release notes and official APIs; implement polite scraping and caching.
- Operational cost of probes vs value: start small (5 providers, 3 regions) and increase only after measurable ROI.

Operational notes and artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MI/pages/Edge+Signal+Cartographer (internal)
- PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-signal-cartographer (PRs: #87, #92)
updates: 2025-02-17 — Liam: Probe matrix approved in kickoff; decided to prioritize NA/EU regions and prioritize short-context (64 tokens) and long-context (2k tokens) synthetic runs.
2025-02-20 — Daniel Kim (Research): Implemented KV-cache-aware probe that measures first-token latency and steady-state per-token latency; PR #87 opened for review.
2025-02-22 — Priya (SRE): Raised concern about probe burstiness affecting provider quotas; agreed to rate-limit probes and stagger windows; added circuit-breaker in CronJob.
2025-02-27 — Ava: First internal card generated; highlighted an EU provider transient with 400ms p95 increase during 02/24–02/25; SRE confirmed linked customer incident RED-204.
2025-03-01 — Maria (Sales): Requested evidence kit template for customer-facing summaries; added to acceptance criteria and created sample slide deck.
2025-03-04 — Liam: Pilot checklist updated; scheduled go/no-go review with SRE and Legal on 2025-03-10 to confirm scraping policy and alerting cadence.
comments: Ava (2025-02-18): Need to ensure this program surfaces signals that map to operational actions; otherwise it will create noise.
Priya (2025-02-20): Suggest adding a minimum persistence of 30 minutes for high-severity signals to avoid transient spikes.
Daniel (2025-02-25): Probe runner updated to tag responses with provider-reported model variant; this helps identify variant rollouts vs infra noise.
Liam (2025-03-03): Add a quick triage template for product owners to decide between routing, rollback, or customer outreach.
